title: Monotone Data-Flow State Machine of Kildall's Algorithm in Ruby: Invariant Preservation and Complexity Analysis
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: We present a Ruby implementation of Kildall's monotone data-flow analysis algorithm, formalized as a state machine that preserves lattice-based invariants while traversing a control-flow graph. The design leverages a balanced search structure for node lookup, ensuring that each transfer function application respects the monotonicity property of the underlying lattice. We prove that the algorithm converges to a fixed point in at most $O(|V|\cdot|E|)$ transfer applications, where $|V|$ and $|E|$ denote the number of vertices and edges, respectively, and that each node's OUT value is a superset of its IN value. Static analysis of the source yields a structural complexity of 191 SLOC and 25 function blocks, with asymptotic search and insertion bounds of $O(\log N)$. The implementation is fully reproducible and available at \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/ruby-algorithms-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261114_110227_kildall_s_algorithm}.
